topics.description: Reference parameters, const references, aliasing, and choosing between copying and observing caller-owned objects.

generation_guidance.easy: One clear pass-by-value or unnecessary-copy bug in a short function. The required behavior should reveal why an alias is needed.
generation_guidance.medium: A realistic API with multiple parameters or interacting read/write views where the learner must choose const versus non-const references.
generation_guidance.hard: Reference lifetime, overload/API design, or aliasing interactions that require reasoning across multiple functions without undefined behavior.

topics.description: Automatic object lifetime, lexical scope, deterministic cleanup, and reverse destruction order.

generation_guidance.easy: A single temporary resource lives too long and should be placed in a narrower block.
generation_guidance.medium: Several resources have different useful lifetimes and cleanup must occur before later work.
generation_guidance.hard: Nested scopes or multiple dependent resources require careful lifetime ordering while preserving program behavior.

topics.description: Move construction, ownership transfer, moved-from state, resource identity, and noexcept behavior.

generation_guidance.easy: A small movable type has an obvious ownership transfer bug with one resource-owning member.
generation_guidance.medium: A domain object owns multiple pieces of state and the learner must preserve invariants while transferring ownership.
generation_guidance.hard: A resource-owning class must avoid duplicate allocation, preserve resource identity, leave a valid moved-from object, and satisfy noexcept.

topics.description: Raw pointer syntax, pointee identity, null state, dereference-based access, aliasing, reseating, and lifetime-aware non-owning observation.

generation_guidance.easy: One raw pointer observes or updates one existing object. Use one clear pointer/pointee relationship, no dangling-lifetime scenario, and at most one write-through path.
generation_guidance.medium: Several pointer-state decisions interact: null handling, reseating between existing objects, aliasing, or mutation through a pointer. Keep the pointees alive for the entire operation so lifetime/dangling reasoning is not yet the main challenge.
generation_guidance.hard: Multiple raw pointers may alias the same pointee, mutation through one view must be visible through another, and at least one pointer crosses a pointee lifetime boundary. The exercise must handle the stale/dangling risk safely without dereferencing a dead object.
